Treat every side of the two `Iff`s as independently true; no genuine implication between them is needed.

- Unfold the canonical cones. `pushoutCoconeOfLeftIso` has apex `Z`, with left leg `inv f ≫ g` and central leg `g`. Dually, `pullbackConeOfLeftIso` has apex `Y`, with left projection `g ≫ inv f`. The three displayed equalities therefore follow by simplification of the relevant natural-transformation components.
- For the final existence statement, use the canonical pullback cone when the right map `g` is an isomorphism: its apex is `X`, with projections `𝟙 X` and `f ≫ inv g`. Its standard universal-property lemma supplies `HasPullback f g`.
- Organize the proof by splitting the outer `And` and both `Iff`s. In every implication, discard the hypothesis and establish the target directly using the corresponding component formula or canonical limiting cone.

The essential assumption is precisely `IsIso` on the appropriate leg, which makes the explicit inverse-based pushout or pullback construction available.
